sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 326.8 ± 41 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Functional transducer-coupling assays performed in HEK-293 cells; receptor is surface-expressed and functionally active in signalling assays (L3). Structural studies (L1) also used this tagged receptor successfully.
sites.rationale: C3AR1 has no endogenous signal peptide; residues 1–24 are extracellular (topology landmark) and TM1 begins at residue 25, placing the N-terminus 24 residues from the first TM boundary — well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. An N-terminal FLAG tag (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M) is the only extracellular N-terminal position, so the junction is topology-derived. Python confirmed residue 1 = M. L3 is the primary anchor because it demonstrates surface expression and preserved transducer-coupling function in HEK-293 cells; L1 and L2 independently corroborate the same N-terminal FLAG architecture in full-length membrane-anchored constructs. HEK-293 cells transfected with N-terminal FLAG-tagged human C3aR (WT and mutants) for functional transducer-coupling assays; surface expression of the tagged full-length receptor confirmed. Corroborated by L1 (structural construct with N-terminal FLAG after exogenous HA signal sequence) and L2 (baculovirus expression with same N-terminal FLAG architecture).

sources.claim: Briefly, HEK-293 cells were transfected with 3.5-5 μg of either N-terminal FLAG-tagged human C3aR or mouse C3aR (WT and mutants), along with 3.5 μg of the F22 plasmid (Promega, Cat.

literature_notes: Four ledger lines were evaluated. L1 and L4 both describe the ICL3-BRIL replacement (residues 360–370 per the paper; canonical topology places the intracellular portion at 362–377); this is an intracellular insertion used to lock the receptor in an inactive conformation for structural studies — it is not a surface tag site and is recorded in other_positions. L2 describes a baculovirus/insect-cell purification construct with the same N-terminal FLAG architecture as L3; L3 is preferred as the primary clip because it provides functional validation in a mammalian cell system. No ledger line supports any insertion in ECL1 (85–97), the large ECL2 (160–340), or ECL3 (403–417), so no sites are proposed there.

literature_other_positions.note: ICL3 residues 360–370 (canonical intracellular span 362–377) were replaced by the thermostabilised BRIL protein to lock C3aR in an inactive conformation for cryo-EM structural studies; this is an intracellular insertion, not a surface tag site.
